brief.headline: HBM shortage extends through 2027; hyperscaler capex hits $700B; CoWoS gap narrows to 10% by year-end
brief.summary: <cite index="9-2,9-3">Samsung's semiconductor division posted 53.7 trillion won ($36.1 billion) in Q1 2026 operating profit, while SK hynix reported 52.6 trillion won ($35.5 billion) revenue and 37.6 trillion won ($27.8 billion) operating profit, fueled by HBM sales</cite>. <cite index="6-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026</cite>, while <cite index="14-2,14-7">DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 and NAND jumped 70-75% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="22-5,22-9">The four biggest hyperscalers will spend roughly $700 billion on capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 levels</cite>. <cite index="32-5">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from 20% currently to 10% by end-2026</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs. Samsung. <cite index="43-5">SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025 vs. Samsung's 35%</cite>, and <cite index="9-3,9-10">SK Hynix's Q1 operating profit of 37.6 trillion won was driven largely by HBM sales</cite>. <cite index="47-1">SK Hynix plans ADR listing as early as July, targeting up to $26.5B to fund AI semiconductor expansion</cite>. Samsung is clawing back—<cite index="43-5">customers stated 'Samsung is back' on HBM4</cite>—but execution lag persists. HBM leverage favors Hynix near-term; watch Samsung's HBM4 qualification pace for reversal signal.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="5-5">Bank of America defines 2026 as a 'supercycle similar to the 1990s boom,' forecasting global DRAM revenue to surge 51% and NAND 45% YoY, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively</cite>. <cite index="9-13">Analysts believe this cycle is different, as AI infrastructure consumes hardware at unprecedented rates</cite>. <cite index="14-10,14-12">Meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027, with cloud providers willing to sign multi-quarter agreements to guarantee allocation</cite>. Pricing momentum sustained by <cite index="11-4">DRAM manufacturers reallocating advanced nodes toward server DRAM and HBM for AI demand</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="7-8">Memory shortage allows Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung to hike prices</cite>. <cite index="10-3,10-4">Nvidia testing 16-layer HBM for delivery as early as late 2026, forcing Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron into a race for next-gen AI accelerators</cite>. <cite index="3-3">Samsung expanding HBM production capacity by ~50% in 2026; SK Hynix increasing infrastructure investment by 4x prior guidance</cite>. <cite index="8-3">Intel-SoftBank ZAM memory promises 2-3x HBM3 bandwidth at fraction of cost/energy</cite>—potential share threat mid-2027. <cite index="2-4,2-5">Korean memory maker discussing separating HBM from GPUs via optical links to expand capacity</cite>.

news_pulse.implication: Demand visibility locked through 2027; GPU/HBM supply remains sole gating factor.

news_pulse.implication: Dilution risk if new shares; but validates premium valuation and funds capacity expansion.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="40-5,40-6">Samsung rose 4.5% to 337,000 won on June 15; SK Hynix gained 6.42% to 2.288 million won</cite>, retracing toward prior highs after geopolitical risk fade. <cite index="44-1,44-3">Korea's new 2x single-stock ETFs on Samsung and SK Hynix attracted strong inflows but choppy performance since launch</cite>; daily rebalancing creates pro-cyclical buying pressure on up days. <cite index="45-2,45-3">3x leveraged Samsung (SMG3) and SK Hynix (HNX3) ETPs launched June 12 on LSE</cite>—watch for gamma effects if momentum continues. KOSPI premarket strength suggests risk-on rotation; position for volatility expansion into earnings season.
